title: Consider using {pkgfiles}
description:
The job of the [pkgfiles](https://github.com/krlmlr/pkgfiles) package is to classify files in an R project according to their use. It helps distinguishing R scripts from other files. Using it would relieve {roxygen2md} from the responsibility to enumerate and filter files.

Most useful after https://github.com/krlmlr/pkgfiles/issues/1 is implemented.

Needs some mulling over, shouldn't delay the CRAN release.

title: feature request: adding support for lists
Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Error message
description:
If the `DESCRIPTION` file does not contain `Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)` we get a cryptic error:

```
> roxygen2md::roxygen2md()
Error in roxygen_field_val$markdown : 
  $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
```

Took me a while to debug this, better error message would be nice.

title: roxygen2md converts Rd syntax within R code
description:
Not sure if this qualifies as a bug, but I noticed that `roxygen2md` converts Rd syntax that is present in R _code_ as well as documentation. A reprex:

``` r
setwd(tempdir())
devtools::create("test")
setwd("test")

cat(
  "#' Title",
  "#' ",
  "#' @param x,y Some stuff here, and a random \\code{code tag}",
  "test_fun <- function(x, y) {",
  "paste('\\code{\', x, \'} and \', y, sep = \'\')",
  "}",
  file = "R/test_fun.R",
  sep = "\n"
)

## View function
writeLines(readLines("R/test_fun.R"))
#> #' Title
#> #' 
#> #' @param x,y Some stuff here, and a random \code{code tag}
#> test_fun <- function(x, y) {
#> paste('\code{', x, '} and ', y, sep = '')
#> }

## Convert to md and view
roxygen2md::roxygen2md()
#> Please review the changes carefully!
writeLines(readLines("R/test_fun.R"))
#> #' Title
#> #' 
#> #' @param x,y Some stuff here, and a random `code tag`
#> test_fun <- function(x, y) {
#> paste('`', x, '` and ', y, sep = '')
#> }
```

I would expect the `\code{code tag}` in the documentation to get converted, but not contents of the function. Though in fairness I was warned to review the changes carefully!

This can come up when a function in the package writes Rd style output and gets called by a `\Sexpr` macro, like [these](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/master/R/utilities-help.r) in ggplot2 (which is where I ran into this issue).

title: add transformers for \emph, \bold and \url
description:
Thanks for a useful tool! I added a few extra transformers to catch some common cases in my roxygen documentation and it would be useful if these could be added:

\emph{...} to *...*
\bold{...} to **...**
\url{...} to ...

With these additional transformers, the main thing I had to do manually was transform old markup spread over multiple lines, e.g.

    #' `Boston`, `Cleveland`, `Detroit`, `Milwaukee`, \code{New
    #' York}, `Toronto`. 

Would be even better if the transformers could fix these too!

title: Export utility string to string translation utility
description:
I would love a function `roxygen_text_to_md()` to work with strings directly.

```r
roxygen_text_to_md("And here we have \emph{italics} in some text.")
#> [1] "And here we have *italics* in some text."
```

This would be useful when translating old documentation to markdown when the old documentation needs additional processing before being written into `roxygen2` comments, or when it won't live in `roxygen2` comments (i.e. gets pulled from another file/etc via a `@template` or `@evalRd` tag).
